title: FX month-end fix: equity-hedge rebalancing flow reverts after the 4pm London fix
hypothesis: Claim: on the last trading day of the month, EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY trend into the 16:00 London (WM/R) fix in the direction implied by month-to-date US-vs-foreign equity performance, and that move partially reverses over the following hours. Trade: fade the pre-fix move on the 5m/15m Timeframe from 16:00 London, exit by NY close. Direction signal from a Reference (US500 vs GER40/UK100 month-to-date return), read on closed bars only. Mechanism: foreign holders of US equities hedge FX exposure and rebalance hedges at month-end at the fix; the flow is forced, price-insensitive, and concentrated in a minute window, so price is pushed away from fair value and reverts once the flow is gone. ~12 events/year per pair, so expect an exploratory tier unless pooled across pairs. Data: Pepperstone cTrader 5m (~3y).
source_detail: agent-generated (Claude) from mechanism; literature: Melvin & Prins (2015) 'Equity hedging and exchange rates at the London 4pm fix', J. Financial Markets
verdict: Rejected on Pepperstone 5m, Oct-2023..Sep-2026 (3 of 6 iterations). Month-end pre-fix moves are larger than normal (15.7 vs 10.1bp) so the flow exists, but neither the realised pre-fix move nor the US-vs-foreign MTD equity signal yields a post-fix reversal that pays Razor costs: pooled event study (99 month-ends, EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY) fade +1.1bp gross t=0.5 vs ~0.9bp round-trip cost; equity-implied post-fix return -2.5bp t=-1.1 (wrong sign). No variant survives 2x costs; OOS signs flip vs IS. Evidence tier exploratory (~36 trades/pair). Power caveat: 95% CI on the pooled gross effect is roughly -3..+5.5bp, so a few-bp effect is not excluded — reopen only with much longer 5m history (pre-2015 fix reform vs post) or a quarter-end subset decided in advance.

title: FX Asian-session overshoot: thin-liquidity moves in EUR/GBP pairs revert into London
hypothesis: Claim: in EURUSD/GBPUSD/EURGBP, a move during the Asian session (00:00-07:00 London) larger than k x the pair's ATR, with no scheduled European/US news, is partially retraced between London open and noon. Mechanism: home-market dealers for these currencies are absent during Asia, so liquidity is thin and the temporary price-impact of a given order is larger; when London liquidity arrives, dealers absorb the inventory and the temporary component decays. The edge should be strongest in pairs where neither currency is Asian (so USDJPY/AUDUSD act as a natural control). Risk: genuine news (e.g. Asian-hours political headline) is permanent, not temporary. Data: Pepperstone cTrader 5m.

title: FX bloc crosses: AUDNZD/EURGBP/EURCHF revert from multi-day z-score extremes
hypothesis: Claim: crosses between two economies exposed to the same shocks (AUDNZD commodity bloc, EURGBP, EURCHF) mean-revert on a 1-10 day horizon after a close-to-close move beyond ~2 sigma of a rolling window, on the 4h/1D Timeframe. Mechanism: the common factor (risk appetite, commodity prices, ECB-area growth) dominates both legs, so the cross only carries the idiosyncratic differential, which is small and transient; a stretch from flows (e.g. one-sided hedging, rate-decision repricing) has no fundamental anchor to persist. Counter-mechanism to rule out: genuine policy divergence (RBA vs RBNZ cycles) produces trends, so a regime filter may be needed — that is a second parameter, budget carefully. Caveats: multi-day holds pay/receive carry; Hermes does not auto-model it — set a FinancingModel on the Cost Model or the result is flattering. EURCHF has a 2015 SNB-floor tail event; do not exclude it from the sample.

title: FX Sunday-open gap reverts as weekend-thin liquidity returns
hypothesis: Claim: when a major pair opens on Sunday (~17:00 NY / 22:00 UTC) with a gap from Friday's close of more than k x ATR, the gap is partially filled within the first 24h. Mechanism: the open is quoted by few dealers with wide spreads before Asian liquidity arrives; the first prints overshoot the weekend's news, and the overshoot decays as liquidity returns. Weekend news that is real (elections, central-bank surprises) does not fill — expect a fat left tail. Caveat: the spread at the Sunday open is several times normal; the default Cost Model will understate it, so entry must be delayed to a liquid bar or spread must be modelled explicitly (ADR-0009). Few events/year per pair — pool across the majors.
source_detail: agent-generated (Claude) from mechanism; liquidity argument at the Wellington open

title: FX post-release overshoot: first-minutes move after NFP/CPI partially retraces
hypothesis: Claim: the first 5-15 minutes of a USD pair's reaction to a US NFP or CPI release overshoots, and a fraction retraces over the next 1-2 hours. Mechanism: market makers pull quotes before the print, so the first trades hit an empty book and algorithmic momentum amplifies them; as depth returns, the temporary price-impact component decays. Distinguish from the permanent component, which is the surprise itself — the retrace should be a fraction, not a full fade. Blocker: Hermes has no economic-calendar source. NFP can be approximated as first Friday 08:30 ET; CPI dates cannot be derived reliably without a calendar.

title: S&P 500 index reconstitution: long additions / short deletions around announcement and effective date
hypothesis: Claim: stocks announced as S&P 500 additions earn positive abnormal return from announcement close to effective date (long), and deletions earn negative abnormal return (short), over a horizon of days to ~2 weeks; the question is which leg, if any, still pays and whether it reverses after the effective date. Mechanism: index funds and closet indexers must buy additions / sell deletions at the effective-date close, price-insensitive and known in advance; arbitrageurs front-run it and demand liquidity from the forced buyers, so price is pushed away from fair value and (partially) reverts after. Literature (Harris-Gurel 1986, Shleifer 1986; later work) finds the addition effect has shrunk and the permanent component faded as it became crowded, while deletions are noisier and often rebound; test each leg separately, and split pre-announcement drift, announcement-to-effective drift, and post-effective reversal as three distinct windows. Data: Hermes has a Constituent Calendar (membership_window per Symbol) but it gives membership dates, not announcement dates, so effective date is the only reliable anchor; announcement ~5 days prior is an approximation. Short leg on deletions needs borrow/financing in the Cost Model. Universe-scale, so needs a build_universe_backtest and the CLI cannot run it yet (CLAUDE.md). Events ~20-25 additions/yr, so pool across years; expect exploratory tier on short samples. Deletions often delist/are acquired, so survivorship in price data is a risk for the short leg.

title: Gold 1h trend-structure breakout: trade breaks of the latest swing in the direction of HH/HL (LH/LL) structure
hypothesis: Claim: on XAUUSD 1h, when swing structure is an uptrend (latest swing high > previous swing high AND latest swing low > previous swing low), a close/touch above the latest swing high continues higher over the following hours; mirror for downtrend (LH+LL) with a break of the latest swing low. Trade only with the structure; no counter-trend breaks. Mechanism: a confirmed higher-high/higher-low sequence marks a directional flow (macro/real-yield repricing, safe-haven or central-bank demand) executed over many hours; a break of the latest swing high is where resting stops and breakout orders cluster, and the stop-driven flow plus trend-followers add to the move, so continuation after a with-trend break should beat a break against structure. Counter-mechanism: gold is range-bound much of the time and swing breaks are the classic false-breakout spot (stop runs, London/NY liquidity sweeps), so the edge may exist only in trending regimes. Quantification notes: swing definition (fractal width n bars) is the main tunable, budget it as a Parameter (k<=3 total; prefer hard-coded n); swings must be confirmed with n bars of lag so a swing is known only after it closes (ADR-0002, no look-ahead); fills next-open / OHLC-touch, Stop-first (ADR-0004); stop at the opposite swing or ATR-based; judge with walk-forward, not whole-sample. Data: Pepperstone cTrader XAUUSD 1h (confirm symbol and depth, cf. NAS100 ~3y of 5m). Include session/spread cost (dynamic spreads) since gold spread is wide around rollover.

Mechanism: a break into new multi-day territory is range expansion with no overhead daily supply and trapped shorts; a break deep inside yesterday's range is intraday noise inside a range. Evidence so far: IS 2018-22 +0.091 ATR4h/trade (n 1599, excess +0.094 t 2.7, 3/5 yrs); holdout 2023-26.08 +0.059 (n 1148, excess +0.037 t 0.95, 2x costs +0.045, 3/4 yrs); rest -0.001. Not the Tokyo breakout (non-Tokyo-edge holdout +0.050). Found by searching 24 features (~85 IS readings, 7 holdout touches on this data) -> the 2023-26 holdout is spent; next evidence must be post-2026-08-06 data or a second instrument (silver), and the rule must be frozen first. Also check whether the fractal is needed at all (plain previous-day-extreme breaks with the same exits).

title: US equity value: long the cheapest S&P 500 names by point-in-time earnings/book yield, rebalanced quarterly
hypothesis: Claim: within the point-in-time S&P 500 calendar universe, stocks in the top quintile of a valuation yield (E/P or B/P from the latest SEC filing known as of the rebalance date, via MassiveFundamentals filing_date) outperform the equal-weight universe over the following 3-12 months; trade it as an equal-weight long-only top-quintile basket rebalanced quarterly (a long/short version vs the bottom quintile is the purer test). Mechanism: investors extrapolate past growth and distress, so recently disappointing, unglamorous firms get priced too cheaply and glamour stocks too dearly; mean reversion in fundamentals then rerates them (LSV). The alternative explanation is a distress-risk premium (Fama-French), which predicts the excess return is real but comes with deep drawdowns in crises. Known caveats to test, not assume away: the US value premium was weak to negative ~2007-2020, so the window chosen matters a lot; must use filing_date not period end (look-ahead); delisted names must stay in (survivorship) - the sp500 calendar handles membership but bars/fundamentals for delisted tickers need checking. Parameters: 1 (the yield metric choice is the variant axis; quintile and quarterly rebalance are fixed constants).
source_detail: Academic value literature: Fama & French (1992, 1993) HML; Lakonishok, Shleifer & Vishny (1994) 'Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation, and Risk'. User asked to try a value strategy on US stocks (2026-10-14).
verdict: Rejected in-sample (2011-2021) even on survivor-biased, value-favouring data (yfinance-only, 201 delisted names unpriced). Top-quintile E/P, B/P and E/P+B/P combo all ~10.5-10.8% CAGR / Sharpe ~0.6 vs 16.1% / 0.93 for the equal-weight benchmark (3 trials). Quintile sorts: no monotonic premium (E/P Q1 -0.36%/qtr vs EW; B/P most-expensive Q5 +0.87%/qtr); sector-neutral ranking worse; cheap-and-profitable did worse than cheap-and-loss-making; value won only in 2013/2016/2020 rotations. Holdout 2022-2026 not touched (no candidate survived). Not worth paying Tiingo to remove a bias that already flatters value. title: US equity value with intangibles: book + capitalized R&D (and organization capital) to market, S&P 500, quarterly
hypothesis: Claim: on the point-in-time S&P 500, ranking by intangible-adjusted book-to-market -- (book equity + capitalised R&D [+ capitalised 30% of SG&A as organization capital]) / market cap, from SEC filings filed by the rebalance date -- gives a top quintile that beats the equal-weight universe over 2011-2021, where plain B/P (idea 21060772) did not. Mechanism: GAAP expenses R&D and brand/organization spending, so book equity omits the main assets of knowledge-economy firms; plain B/P therefore labels intangible-heavy firms expensive and loads on asset-heavy, declining firms. Correcting the denominator should restore value's original meaning (cheap relative to productive capital). Falsifier: if adjusted B/P does no better than plain B/P in-sample, mis-measurement is not why value failed here. Constants (not knobs): R&D and org capital depreciate 20%/yr (BEA-style), 30% of SG&A is investment (EKP), initial stock = first observed flow / (depreciation + 10% growth). Parameters: 1 (metric).
source_detail: Lev & Srivastava (2019) 'Explaining the Recent Failure of Value Investing'; Eisfeldt, Kim & Papanikolaou (2020) 'Intangible Value'; Peters & Taylor (2017) for the perpetual-inventory capitalisation. Follow-up to rejected idea 21060772 (plain B/P lost to equal weight 2011-2021). Prompted by Ilmanen, Expected Returns.
verdict: Rejected in-sample (2011-2021, survivor-biased yfinance-only data that favours value). Capitalising R&D (+30% SG&A) moved results the predicted way but not enough: top-quintile backtests 11.0% (ibp) / 11.2% (ibp_org) CAGR vs 10.8% plain B/P vs 16.1% equal weight (2 trials). Quintile sorts: cheapest-quintile excess vs EW -0.17 -> -0.02 -> +0.08%/qtr (t~0.1); improvement over plain B/P +0.25%/qtr, t=1.3; ex-financials +0.24%/qtr t=0.4. What it does explain: the cheap-minus-expensive spread shrinks from -1.09 to -0.21%/qtr ex-financials, i.e. mis-measured intangibles account for much of why glamour beat value here, but no value premium appears. Only suggestive pocket: manufacturing (+0.68%/qtr vs plain B/P, t=1.5), not pursued (narrowing the universe on a t<2 cut is search). Holdout 2022+ untouched.

title: US equity value + momentum: 50/50 combination of the cheapest and the strongest-trending S&P 500 quintiles, quarterly
hypothesis: Claim: on the point-in-time S&P 500, a 50/50 portfolio of the cheapest B/P quintile and the top 12-1 month momentum quintile (rebalanced quarterly) has a higher Sharpe than momentum alone and than the equal-weight universe over 2011-2021, because the two sleeves' excess returns are negatively correlated. Mechanism: momentum buys what has risen (often expensive), value buys what has fallen (often cheap), so they hold opposite stocks; momentum crashes are sharp reversals into beaten-down stocks, which is exactly when value pays. The combination earns a premium from diversification even if value's own premium is ~0 (as found in 21060772/f99af81f). Falsifier: if the quarterly excess returns of the value and momentum sleeves are not clearly negatively correlated in-sample (rho > -0.2), the diversification case fails here and the combo is just a diluted momentum book. Constants: 12-1 month lookback (252 minus 21 trading days), quintiles, quarterly, 50/50. Parameters: 1 (metric).
source_detail: Ilmanen, Expected Returns (2011), value chapter: value and momentum negatively correlated, so the combination beats either; Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere'; Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) for 12-1 momentum. Follows rejected value ideas 21060772 and f99af81f.
verdict: Rejected in-sample (2011-2021, S&P 500, survivor-biased yfinance-only data). The diversification half of the claim holds: value and momentum quintiles' quarterly excess returns correlate -0.55 (long-short -0.73); momentum's worst quarters (Q3/Q4 2020) were value's best (+10-15%), and 50/50 cuts excess vol from 2.6-4.5 to ~1.9%/qtr and the worst quarter from -6/-14% to -4.7%. But neither sleeve had a premium here: momentum top quintile -0.54%/qtr vs EW quarterly-rebalanced, -0.08%/mo (t -0.5) monthly; value ~0 (ideas 21060772, f99af81f). Combining two ~zero-premium sleeves gives a low-tracking-error ~zero premium: backtests mom 11.6% CAGR / Sharpe 0.70, 50/50 bp+mom 11.1% / 0.68, 50/50 ibp_org+mom 11.5% / 0.71, vs EW 16.1% / 0.93 (3 trials). Holdout untouched. Large-cap US 2011-2021 may simply be the wrong place: AMP's evidence is long-short across many markets and asset classes.

title: S&P 500 volatile-dip limit buy: >3% down day in an uptrend, limit 0.9 ATR(5) below, short-hold rebound exit
hypothesis: Claim: within the point-in-time S&P 500 calendar universe on daily bars, a stock above its 200-day SMA that closes down >3% vs the prior close (signal day) with 100*ATR(5)/Close > 3, bought next day with a limit order 0.9*ATR(5) below the signal-day close, rebounds within days: exit on the first close above the previous day's high, or at a profit target of the previous close + 0.5*ATR(5) (from the day after entry), or after 10 trading days. When several signals compete for capital in one pool, take the highest ATR(5)/Close first. Net of costs it beats (a) the equal-weight universe and (b) random entries on random uptrend days held with the same exits. Mechanism: in an established uptrend a sharp one- or two-day selloff is mostly liquidity-driven (forced or impatient sellers, stop cascades, de-risking, overreaction to news), not information that breaks the trend. Liquidity providers who buy that capitulation are paid a short-term reversal premium. The deeper limit entry buys only on days the selling extends into a second session, which is when the premium is largest, and the ATR scaling makes 'deep' comparable across names. The high-volatility ranking concentrates on the names where the overshoot is largest. Counter: the short-term reversal premium has decayed since the 1990s and is concentrated in small, illiquid names, so S&P 500 large caps may be too efficient. A dip that continues through a limit that sits far below the close is adverse selection: fills happen most often on the days the news is real (earnings misses), so the falling-knife tail must be measured, not assumed away. Mean-reversion edges are short-vol and lose in crashes (2008, 2020, 2022). Testing hazards: survivorship (use the sp500 calendar universe with delisted names kept); limit fills (OHLC-touch fills at the limit when low <= limit, but a gap down below the limit should fill at the open, ADR-0004, and touch-only fills flatter the result, so also measure fills that need the low to trade through by a tick); the 'previous close + 0.5 ATR' target is ambiguous (the entry day's close vs the signal close), so pin one; earnings gaps; the many fixed constants (3%, 3 vol, 0.9, 0.5, 10 days, 200 SMA) are book values to be hard-coded, not tuned, and at most one (the limit depth) is a declared Parameter. Protocol: choose on an early window, score a later window once, 2x costs, random-entry baseline with identical exits, regime split (2008/2020/2022). Note: analyze on universe runs measures only trades/validation/regime/gate today, so costs/params/oos need the event-study or a per-symbol path.
